items.title: Drame en Guinée: Quatre orpailleurs burkinabè tués par la foudre dans une mine d’or à Siguiri
items.description: La série noire se poursuit dans la zone aurifère de la préfecture de Doko. Dans la soirée du jeudi 3 septembre 2026, la foudre a mortellement frappé quatre orpailleurs de nationalité burkinabè alors qu’ils travaillaient dans une mine d’or artisanale. Ce terrible accident, qui a également fait un blessé, illustre une nouvelle fois la vulnérabilité extrême des mineurs artisanaux face aux violentes intempéries de la saison pluvieuse et repose l'épineuse question des mesures de prévention sur les sites d'exploitation. Le drame s’est noué aux environs de 19 heures, ce jeudi 3 septembre 2026, sous des pluies diluviennes qui s'abattaient sur le district de Sèkè Gbédégbè, une localité située à quelque 55 kilomètres de Siguiri-ville. En pleine activité d'orpaillage au sein d'une exploitation artisanale en brousse, un groupe de mineurs de nationalité burkinabè a été surpris par une décharge électrique atmosphérique d'une violence inouïe. Le bilan est lourd : quatre hommes ont été tués sur le coup, tandis qu'un autre a été blessé. Faute de réseau ou de téléphone à proximité immédiate pour donner l'alerte au moment de l'orage, ce n'est que le lendemain matin que les populations locales et les autorités ont été informées de la tragédie. Interrogé sur les circonstances matérielles exactes — notamment la manipulation éventuelle d'objets métalliques par les victimes —, un acteur local a refusé d'apporter plus de précisions. L’unique rescapé blessé a quant à lui été évacué d'urgence vers le centre de santé de Doko où il reçoit actuellement des soins. Dès la découverte du sinistre, la population s'est mobilisée. Les corps des quatre orpailleurs décédés ont été officiellement remis à la communauté et aux familles burkinabè en vue de leur inhumation, après avoir obtenu l'autorisation formelle du procureur de la République de Guinée. Pour ces familles immigrées venues chercher fortune dans les gisements d'or guinéens, la douleur est immense et le deuil s'organise dans la dignité. Ce nouveau décès collectif n'est malheureusement pas un cas isolé. La région administrative de Siguiri paie un tribut de plus en plus lourd à la saison pluvieuse actuelle. Quelques jours seulement avant ce drame, la commune urbaine de Doko avait déjà été endeuillée par la mort d'une fillette d'une dizaine d'années, foudroyée dans un accident qui avait également fait deux blessés parmi les orpailleurs burkinabè. Au total, les données locales révèlent qu’une dizaine de personnes ont déjà perdu la vie dans la zone à la suite de foudroiements depuis le début de la saison des pluies. Cette répétition tragique suscite une vive inquiétude au sein des exploitations artisanales. Travaillant en brousse et fortement exposés aux décharges électriques, les orpailleurs continuent trop souvent leurs activités malgré les risques majeurs liés aux orages. Pour les acteurs de la société civile, ce drame doit impérativement servir de déclic pour renforcer les campagnes de sensibilisation et mettre en place des mesures de prévention rigoureuses afin d'éviter que la quête de l'or ne se transforme en arrêt de mort. L’article Drame en Guinée: Quatre orpailleurs burkinabè tués par la foudre dans une mine d'or à Siguiri est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Percée historique de l’extrême droite en Allemagne : l’Europe face à ses démons
items.description: Pour la première fois depuis la Seconde Guerre mondiale, un Land (région) en Allemagne pourrait être dirigé par un parti d’extrême droite, autrement dit néonazi. La menace du retour du fascisme au pouvoir sur le Vieux Continent n’a jamais été aussi pesante depuis huit décennies. Signe qui ne trompe pas quant à la gravité de la situation, même une partie de l’extrême droite française a exprimé son inquiétude après le tsunami électoral de l’AfD dans un Land de l’est de l’Allemagne. Allemagne : la victoire de l’extrême droite dans le Land de Saxe-Anhalt suscite de vives inquiétudes Dimanche 6 septembre, le parti extrémiste a remporté les élections législatives régionales en Saxe-Anhalt, un Land situé sur le territoire de l’ex-RDA. L’AfD a réalisé un score qu’aucun autre parti n’a réalisé auparavant : 44,8% des voix, ce qui le met à trois sièges seulement de la majorité absolue au Parlement régional. L’onde de choc a atteint toute l’Europe car il s’agit de l’Allemagne, qui constitue le plus grand État de l’Union européenne et qui a connu la montée du nazisme dans les années 1930 et 1940 avec les conséquences que l’on sait pour toute l’humanité. Si le pays tombe dans l’escarcelle des néonazis, les autres pourraient le suivre comme des dominos. L'Italie est déjà gouvernée par l’extrême droite depuis 2022. La France pourrait très probablement suivre dès l’année prochaine. D’autres gouvernements européens sont formés par des coalitions comptant des partis extrémistes. “Un moment grave en Europe” Cela ne semblait pas poser problème tant que la xénophobie de ce courant se limitait aux immigrés et aux musulmans. Avec le risque de voir l’Allemagne basculer dans l’extrémisme, le danger est pris au sérieux. Le gouvernement français a déploré par la voix de son ministre chargé de l’Europe, Benjamin Haddad, “un moment grave en Europe”. Jean-Luc Mélenchon a anticipé une remilitarisation de l’Allemagne indiquant que, “dans ces conditions, le projet militaire allemand de créer la première armée conventionnelle d’Europe est inacceptable pour la France”. Pour le président du gouvernement espagnol Pedro Sanchez, ce qui s’est passé dimanche en Saxe “montre clairement que la menace d’extrême droite gagne du terrain en Europe et dans le monde”. Lo que vimos ayer en Sajonia es un aviso de que la amenaza ultra gana terreno en Europa y el mundo. Y también la constatación de que un gobierno de coalición progresista es más necesario que nunca. Los datos nos avalan. Llevamos 8 años y, el año que viene, otros 4 años más. pic.twitter.com/21Z2zugJo6 — Pedro Sánchez (@sanchezcastejon) September 7, 2026 Le premier secrétaire du Parti socialiste (PS) français Olivier Faure a souligné un détail qui est peut-être annonciateur de quelque chose de plus grave : le Land de Saxe-Anhalt fut le premier à élire un ministre-président nazi en 1932. Un an après, c’est Hitler qui a pris le pouvoir. “Ce n’est plus un avertissement, c’est un ordre de mobilisation générale qu’il faut lancer”, a-t-il écrit sur X . Vers une prise de conscience collective ? Alors que Dominique de Villepin a souligné que la victoire de l'AfD est le signe que les “digues sautent les unes après les autres (…) avec une régularité qui devrait tous nous alarmer”, Robert Ménard, figure connue de l’extrême droite, s’est dit “effrayé” et “inquiet” du fait “qu’on en arrive à voter pour des nazillons”. Les propos du maire de Béziers, un farouche anti-immigration, sont un signe que l’heure est grave. Même Éric Zemmour et Sarah Knafo n'ont pas franchement applaudi, se contentant d'expliquer le vote des Allemands par leur ras-le-bol des politiques suivies jusque-là notamment en matière d’immigration. L’éventualité du retour du nazisme en Allemagne sème la panique en Europe, particulièrement en France où même l’extrême droite peine à cacher son inquiétude. L’occasion peut-être pour une prise de conscience collective que continuer à instrumentaliser les questions identitaires, c’est jouer avec le feu. Car le retour en force de l’extrême droite au pouvoir dans un pays comme l’Allemagne est avant tout un problème pour l’Europe. L’article Percée historique de l'extrême droite en Allemagne : l'Europe face à ses démons est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: La RDC accélère ses exportations de cuivre vers les États-Unis, tandis que la Chine reste son principal débouché
items.description: Les echanges entre la RDC et les etats-Unis ont nettement accelere depuis le debut de l'annee. Entre janvier et juillet 2026, les importations americaines de marchandises en provenance du pays ont atteint 2,123 milliards de dollars, contre 1,281 milliard sur la meme periode en 2025. En seulement sept mois, elles depassent deja les 1,928 milliards enregistres sur l'ensemble de 2025. Le cuivre est au cœur de cette progression. Au premier semestre 2026, environ 1,04 milliard de dollars sur les 1,411 milliard de produits congolais importes par les etats-Unis concernaient le cuivre et les produits en cuivre. La tendance s'est encore renforcee en juillet. Les etats-Unis ont importe un record de 53 290 tonnes de cathodes de cuivre congolais, soit 23,9 % de leurs importations de cuivre du mois. Le changement d'echelle est rapide : en 2024, les etats-Unis avaient importe moins de 32 000 tonnes de cuivre congolais sur toute l'annee. En 2025, la RDC etait deja devenue leur deuxieme fournisseur de cuivre raffine, avec environ 187 000 tonnes, derriere le Chili. Kinshasa cherche a elargir sa marge de manœuvre Cette hausse s'inscrit dans la strategie de diversification engagee par Kinshasa, qui cherche a reduire sa dependance a un nombre limite de circuits commerciaux et a mieux valoriser ses ressources minieres. Gecamines, l'entreprise miniere publique congolaise, joue un role central dans cette evolution en renforcant son controle sur la commercialisation d'une partie des volumes issus de ses participations minieres. En janvier, le groupe a ainsi exerce son droit d'achat sur 100 000 tonnes de la production 2026 de Tenke Fungurume, une importante mine de cuivre et de cobalt en RDC. Ces volumes sont destines au marche americain avec l'appui de Mercuria, un groupe international specialise dans le negoce de matieres premieres, qui fournit un soutien financier, logistique et technique. Le cuivre congolais est egalement davantage accepte par les industriels americains. Aucune marque produite en RDC n'est actuellement agreee pour livraison sur le COMEX, le marche americain de reference pour les contrats a terme sur les metaux. Le cuivre congolais est toutefois generalement vendu sur la base des cours du London Metal Exchange, ou LME, l'un des principaux marches mondiaux de reference pour les metaux industriels, parfois avec une decote. Cette difference peut le rendre moins coûteux pour certains acheteurs, tandis que l'amelioration de sa qualite a renforce son acceptation sur le marche americain. La Chine conserve une place centrale La progression americaine ne modifie toutefois pas la hierarchie des debouches du cuivre congolais. La Chine reste le principal marche. Sur les sept premiers mois de 2026, les importations chinoises de cuivre provenant de RDC ont recule de 4,3 %, mais le pays representait encore 44,7 % des importations chinoises de cuivre. En juillet, la Chine en a importe 95 778 tonnes, contre 53 290 tonnes pour les etats-Unis. La hausse des flux vers les etats-Unis apparaît donc davantage comme une diversification des exportations congolaises que comme un basculement strategique vers le marche americain. Le record enregistre en juillet doit aussi etre relativise, une partie des achats ayant ete realisee en anticipation de possibles droits de douane. La RDC cherche ainsi a multiplier ses debouches et a conserver une plus grande autonomie commerciale, tout en maintenant des echanges importants avec son principal marche asiatique.

items.title: Dangote targets 10m shareholders as Refinery IPO opens
items.description: By Olakunle Oke, Marvellous Uzoma and Kamsy Gbenoba The Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals has commenced its Initial Public Offering (IPO), with President of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, targeting 10 million shareholders across Africa in what he described as an “IPO for the people.” The refinery is offering its shares at N525 each, with a minimum subscription of 10 shares, as it seeks to raise more than N2 trillion to fund its expansion programme. However, Dangote said raising capital was not the primary motivation for taking the refinery to the public market, stressing that the business was already generating strong free cash flow and had previously accessed significant funding through bonds and private placements. He said the IPO was primarily designed to broaden ownership of the multibillion-naira refinery and give ordinary Nigerians and other Africans an opportunity to participate in its future growth. “We want to get as many Africans as possible. We are targeting 10 million shareholders from all over Africa and maybe other parts of the world,” Dangote said. He urged investors to participate according to their financial capacity, saying those who could afford the minimum 10 shares should invest at that level, while investors with greater capacity could subscribe for substantially more. Dangote said the offering was intended to cut across income and professional groups, including employees such as drivers, cooks, managers and other workers. “We want this to be an IPO for the people,” he said, adding that wider ownership would help spread the benefits of the refinery across society. He said the investment could provide ordinary salary earners with an avenue to build long-term wealth and secure the future of their families, particularly through investments that could support education and other needs. Dangote also expressed the hope that the IPO would create more millionaires across Africa, drawing comparisons with early investors in companies such as Amazon who benefited from the long-term growth of their investments. Beyond the refinery, he said the Dangote Group’s fertiliser business and other industrial operations could provide additional opportunities for Africans to participate in the continent’s industrial transformation. Dangote said the valuation and pricing of the IPO were based on normal business conditions and were not built around exceptional profits arising from geopolitical crises, including the Middle East conflict or the Russia-Ukraine war. He said the refinery’s financial projections were based on its expected performance under normal market conditions rather than temporary supply disruptions or unusually high international energy prices. “We don’t base our business on crisis. We base our businesses on a normal trend. Whatever we have over and above that is icing on the cake,” he said. Dangote warned investors and businesses against building long-term strategies around temporary geopolitical disruptions, noting that conflicts would eventually end and markets would return to normal conditions. He described the refinery as a long-term, multigenerational investment that should continue operating for decades. The Dangote Refinery currently has a stated refining capacity of 700,000 barrels per day, positioning it among the world’s largest single-train refining facilities and as a major supplier of refined petroleum products to Nigeria and international markets. The company has also emerged as a significant supplier of aviation fuel to international markets, including Europe. Under its expansion programme, the refinery plans to double its capacity to 1.4 million barrels per day, while expanding its petrochemical and petroleum products distribution operations across Africa. The expansion is targeted for completion by 2028 and is expected to further strengthen the refinery’s position as an integrated refining and petrochemical complex. The company also plans to expand its distribution infrastructure across West Africa, including proposed tank farms and pipeline operations in Namibia to improve the movement of petroleum products to underserved inland markets. Dangote said the long-term objective was to transform the refinery into a pan-African energy platform capable of supporting energy security, industrialisation and economic growth across the continent. He argued that the project had demonstrated that African businesses could execute large-scale industrial projects capable of competing in global markets. Dangote commended the refinery’s bankers, advisers, regulators, the Nigerian Exchange Group and other stakeholders for their roles in bringing the IPO to the market. He described the offering as the biggest IPO in Africa’s history and urged Nigerians and other African investors to take advantage of the opportunity to become shareholders in the refinery. The IPO marks a significant new phase for the Dangote Refinery, combining an ambitious expansion programme with an effort to distribute ownership of one of Africa’s largest industrial projects among millions of investors. items.title: Hearts coach Kapor tips Alex Banso for Ghana football stardom
items.description: Hearts of Oak head coach Nebojsa Kapor has backed Alex Banso to become a future star of Ghana football, while urging fans and the media to give the youngster time to develop. Banso played a key role in Hearts’ impressive 4-0 victory over Berekum Chelsea, providing an assist as the Phobians opened their campaign with a commanding win. The youngster’s performance has impressed Kapor, who believes his versatility and composure could make him an important player for both Hearts and Ghana in the years ahead. “He’s a future of Ghana football, and I want Ghanaians to be calm with him,” Kapor said. The Serbian coach has called for patience, warning against putting unnecessary pressure on the young midfielder as he continues his development. “He is a young, good player and he can operate from all positions that are close to dangerous areas,” he added. “He is very good and very calm boy, which is very good for him. But I am also begging you to calm down and let’s see. I am praying we will get from him in the future.” Kapor also credited Hearts’ intensive training programme for Banso’s performance, highlighting the work being done to prepare the squad for the new season.

items.title: Culture : la date de la saison culturelle de la ville marocaine d’Assilla fixée au 2 octobre prochain
items.description: La ville marocaine d'Assilla se prépare à organiser la 49e édition de sa Saison culturelle internationale, du 2 au 18 octobre 2026, conformément au programme annoncé par la Fondation Forum d'Assilla. Le programme de la saison comprend des colloques et des manifestations culturelles et intellectuelles abordant un certain nombre de questions politiques, intellectuelles et culturelles, parmi lesquelles les enjeux énergétiques et hydriques en Afrique et les projets stratégiques, vers une nouvelle géographie politique africaine, thème du colloque d’ouverture prévu les 2 et 3 octobre. Le programme comprend également une conférence sur « Tony Marini et la scène artistique marocaine » les 5 et 6 octobre, ainsi qu’une conférence intitulée « Le monde arabe à l’horizon 2030 : défis, mutations et perspectives » les 10 et 11 du même mois. La saison consacre une partie de son programme à la littérature et à la poésie, à travers la « Tente de la création » qui accueille un événement consacré à l’écrivain marocain Mbarek Rabie, intitulé « L’authenticité de l’écrivain et les chemins de l’écriture », ainsi qu’une conférence intitulée « Hassouna Al-Masbahi… Mon voyage à travers les expressions et les lieux ». Le programme comprend également une table ronde consacrée aux nouveaux poètes du monde arabe et à l’évolution de la poésie, de la pluralité des formes à l’intermédiarité, ainsi que l’organisation de la huitième édition du Prix Blend Al-Haidari destiné aux jeunes poètes arabes. La saison culturelle internationale d’Assilla s’achèvera le 18 octobre par une cérémonie de clôture, après plus de deux semaines d’activités, de conférences et d’événements culturels et intellectuels.

items.title: Interpol Pakistan issues 286 red notices in 7 months, 53 fugitives repatriated
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Interpol’s National Central Bureau (NCB) in Pakistan issued 286 Red Notices in the last seven months as part of efforts to track fugitives involved in murder, fraud, terrorism and human trafficking, according to Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) Director General Dr Usman Anwar. A Red Notice is a request to law enforcement agencies by Interpol to locate and provisionally arrest a person pending extradition, surrender or similar legal action. Anwar, who also heads NCB-Interpol Pakistan, reaffirmed the agency’s resolve on World Day of International Police Cooperation, adding that Islamabad would continue to strengthen collaboration with Interpol and global partners. NCBs serve as each country’s focal point for all Interpol activities. They connect national law enforcement agencies with those in other countries and with the Interpol General Secretariat through a secure global police communications network known as I-24/7, allowing real-time access to databases and services. Anwar said NCB-Interpol Pakistan issued a total of 290 Interpol notices during the period, including two Blue Notices and two Yellow Notices. Yellow Notices are meant to help locate missing persons, often minors, or identify people who are unable to identify themselves, while Blue Notices are issued to collect additional information. Of the 286 Red Notices, 225 were issued for suspects wanted in murder and attempted murder cases, while another 33 were issued for individuals wanted in kidnapping, corruption, robbery and cybercrime cases. The bureau also issued 19 Red Notices for financial fraud and deception, six for human trafficking and three for terrorism. Through international cooperation, 53 fugitives wanted in Pakistan for serious crimes were arrested in different countries and extradited to Pakistan during the same seven-month period. “Today’s crimes are increasingly international. Cybercrime, fugitives and stolen goods driven by organised groups — none of these respect borders,” Anwar told Dawn . “We seek information from other NCBs to help investigations in Pakistan, and we share our criminal data to assist other countries.” He added that NCBs were critical because they could trigger law enforcement action in their respective countries and work directly with counterparts, even between states without diplomatic relations. “When a crime goes beyond our national jurisdiction, we need international support to solve it. Interpol provides that platform,” he stated. According to Interpol’s framework, NCBs contribute national crime data to global databases in accordance with national laws. Red Notices, for example, alert police in all 196 member countries to wanted persons. NCB Pakistan works with domestic law enforcement agencies, other NCBs and sub-bureaus worldwide, as well as the General Secretariat’s offices, to coordinate cross-border investigations, operations and arrests. The FIA director general noted that regional cooperation was growing as countries combined resources to tackle shared threats. “We are also building capacity at home. NCBs develop training programmes for national police to raise awareness of Interpol’s tools and databases so that our officers can use them effectively on the ground,” Anwar said. “FIA NCB-Interpol Pakistan remains committed to ensuring that no fugitive finds safe haven abroad. Through I-24/7 and our network of partners, we will keep pursuing criminals and bringing them to justice.” In April this year, Interpol issued Red Notices against Bahria Town owner Malik Riaz and his son Ali Riaz, Nat­i­onal Accountability Bur­eau (NAB) Chairman Lt General (retired) Nazir Ahmed said. Last month, the National Cybercrime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) arrested two suspects and initiated the process for obtaining Red Notices for the remaining four alleged members of the “Tycoon2FA Cybercrime Network”.

items.title: Nasarawa SDP crisis deepens as Ajegena moves to control secretariat
items.description: By Edwin Phillip, Lafia LAFIA — The leadership crisis rocking the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Nasarawa State deepened on Monday as the party’s state chairman, Barrister Ibrahim Likita Ajegena, said he had assumed control of the party secretariat in Lafia. Ajegena also declared that the party was prepared to wrest power from the ruling party in the state and at the centre in the 2027 general elections. Addressing journalists against the backdrop of the lingering disagreement within the Nasarawa SDP, Ajegena dismissed reports of a serious crisis, describing those challenging his leadership as “aggrieved members” who had allegedly resorted to what he termed “spoiler” activities after failing to achieve their objectives within the party. “There is no crisis in the SDP. There are only some aggrieved members who feel that they could not do anything but to become spoilers,” Ajegena said. He insisted that the party remained functional despite the disagreement and had continued to operate through its zonal offices across the state. The chairman said his move to reclaim the official state secretariat, located along Jos Road, opposite the Catholic Church in Lafia, was a signal that the party had entered a new phase and would not allow internal disagreements to derail its preparations for the 2027 elections. His return to the secretariat came barely two days after the SDP conducted a substitution primary across Nasarawa State, producing former Inspector-General of Police, Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, as its governorship candidate for the 2027 election following the withdrawal of Musa Adamu Angba. The primary was conducted across the state’s 13 local government areas, with 28,637 delegates participating, according to the SDP Electoral Committee. Adamu, who was the sole aspirant in the exercise, emerged as the party’s candidate after securing the highest number of valid votes. Reacting to the turnout, Ajegena described the large crowd at the exercise as a warning to rival political parties, saying it demonstrated growing acceptance of the SDP among residents of the state. “What we witnessed on Saturday is a sign of victory. The crowd was massive and it showed that the people are with us,” he said. Ajegena said the SDP would immediately intensify grassroots mobilisation across the 13 local government areas, stressing that the party’s ambition went beyond merely participating in the 2027 elections. “We are battle-ready for 2027. The SDP is prepared to take Nasarawa State, and we are also prepared to take the presidency,” he said. However, the leadership dispute appears unresolved, as a factional chairman of the party, Danlami Musa, who is also chairman of the Inter-Party Advisory Council (IPAC) and belongs to the Shehu Gabam-led group, had also laid claim to the party secretariat. items.title: La Mauritanie met en garde contre un conflit régional généralisé et réaffirme son soutien à la cause palestinienne
items.description: Le ministre des Affaires étrangères, de la Coopération africaine et des Mauritaniens de l'extérieur, Mohamed Salem Ould Merzoug, a déclaré ce lundi que la nation arabe était confrontée à une situation régionale extrêmement délicate, mettant en garde contre les risques d'une dérive vers un conflit régional généralisé. Le ministre s’exprimait lors d’un discours prononcé à l’occasion de la 166e session ordinaire du Conseil de la Ligue des États arabes au niveau des ministres des Affaires étrangères, au Caire. Ould Merzoug a ajouté que la région connaissait des crises sécuritaires et politiques successives, ainsi que des ingérences extérieures qui entravent les efforts de stabilisation et de développement, appelant les États arabes à coordonner leurs positions et à unir leurs efforts pour éviter que le conflit ne s’étende. Le ministre a réaffirmé la position de la Mauritanie en faveur du droit du peuple palestinien à établir son État indépendant dans les frontières du 4 juin 1967, avec Al Qods-Est pour capitale, appelant à un cessez-le-feu immédiat dans la bande de Gaza, à la fin des violations en Cisjordanie et à la fourniture d’un soutien d’urgence pour renforcer la résistance du peuple palestinien. En conclusion de son intervention, il a réaffirmé la volonté de la Mauritanie de soutenir les efforts visant à renforcer la solidarité arabe, à unifier les positions et à relever les défis communs.

items.title: UN Finds Little Progress on Justice in Sri Lanka
items.description: Click to expand Image United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk holds a press conference in Colombo, Sri Lanka, June 26, 2025. © 2025 Krishan Kariyawasam/NurPhoto via AP Photo Seventeen years after the end of Sri Lanka’s civil war, the latest report by the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk, updates the current human rights situation in the country. The government of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake took office in September 2024, promising justice for past rights violations. Yet, as the high commissioner’s September 3 report concludes, beyond progress in a few important cases, “there has been no recognition or accountability for crimes under international law, gross human rights violations, and serious violations of international humanitarian law committed by all parties” during the war with the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam, which ended in 2009. Human Rights Watch raised similar concerns in its September 1 report, which documented limited progress in some emblematic cases, but no movement in cases dealing with enforced disappearances, the killing of aid workers, or the targeting of journalists. The government has failed to follow through on its promise to establish an independent public prosecutor’s office, or undertake legal or structural reforms needed for accountability. The Dissanayake government has also not accepted the Sri Lanka Accountability Project, established by the UN Human Rights Council to collect evidence of serious rights abuses. The Sri Lankan government still uses the repressive Prevention of Terrorism Act to harass and arrest human rights defenders, journalists, and families of victims. They face surveillance and questioning by state intelligence agencies, particularly in northern and eastern Sri Lanka. The high commissioner’s report calls on the government to impose a moratorium on using the law pending its repeal, and to release people long detained under it. The Sri Lankan government needs to urgently institute long-pending legal and structural reforms, repeal repressive laws, undertake comprehensive security sector reform, and take steps toward genuine reconciliation, or it risks further entrenching impunity and the trust deficit among victims. The Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights should continue to monitor the Sri Lankan government’s progress on accountability for international crimes. UN member states at the Human Rights Council and other countries should press the Dissanayake government to follow through on its commitments to ensure truth and justice. Two decades on, the families of victims are still waiting.

items.title: “Antoine Semenyo can play nine” – Maresca backs Semenyo to deputise for Haaland
items.description: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has revealed that Ghana forward Antoine Semenyo could be used as a centre-forward during the 2026/27 season as the club looks to manage Erling Haaland’s workload. City travel to Portugal to face FC Porto in the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday, September 8, with Maresca admitting that Haaland will need to be carefully managed during a demanding campaign. The Norwegian striker has played almost every minute for City this season, except for the Community Shield, prompting the manager to consider alternative options in attack. “At the moment, he’s played every minute apart from the Community Shield. We need to protect Erling because the season is very long and he’s going to have games where he needs to recover,” Maresca said. With City unable to add another recognised striker during the transfer window, Semenyo could provide an alternative in the number nine role when Haaland needs a rest. Asked whether the Ghanaian can operate as a centre-forward, Maresca said: “Depends on the game and game plan. Antoine can play nine. It depends on the game.” Semenyo has already made three appearances for City this season and has contributed two assists. His versatility across the front line could prove valuable as City juggle their Premier League, Champions League and domestic cup commitments. The potential role as a centre-forward would also give Semenyo another opportunity to make an impact as he continues to establish himself at the Etihad Stadium.

items.title: King makes clear Harry and Meghan remain non-working royals
items.description: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex will not be working royals allowed to carry out official engagements now they have returned to the UK, a letter sent on behalf of King Charles spells out. The letter is intended to clarify the status of Prince Harry and Meghan, who moved back from California with children Archie and Lilibet last month. They will still not be able to use the “HRH” titles of His and Her Royal Highness, and remain “private citizens”, says the letter sent on behalf of the King by the Lord Chamberlain, a top Palace official. It has been sent to Prince Harry’s team, government departments, military officials and Lord Lieutenants, according to Palace sources. Lord Lieutenants, who are the monarch’s local representatives, and government staff are often involved in royal visits and engagements. This letter makes clear that any engagements carried out by the Sussexes will be in a private capacity and they will not be representing the Royal Family. It seems to be something of a shot across the bows, making clear that any Prince Harry and Meghan visits should not be treated as royal engagements. This comes ahead of what are likely to be public appearances by the Sussexes this autumn, as they settle in the UK and support their charities. The message from the King emphasises that the position agreed in 2020 when the Sussexes left the UK – the so-called Sandringham Agreement – is still in place. This ruled out any “half-in and half-out” status, so Harry and Meghan could not pursue their own commercial interests while continuing to be working royals. “It is well known that in January 2020 the Duke and Duchess stepped down from undertaking representative duties on behalf of the Sovereign, and are no longer working members of the Royal Family,” the letter says. The letter sent on behalf of the King makes it clear that this remains the case. “The charitable work of the Duke and Duchess is a personal matter for them both and undertaken in their private capacity,” it adds. The King’s message says that any questions from organisations about the reception to be given to the Sussexes, “particularly where recourse to public funds may be required, should be directed to Buckingham Palace”. Prince Harry and Meghan faced an acrimonious departure from the UK in 2020, which they chronicled in their Netflix documentary. They established their financial independence in California, including Prince Harry writing a best-selling memoir Spare and Meghan creating an online food range, As Ever. This summer the couple made a surprise return to the UK, where their children will be going to school. It’s expected that Prince Harry will be supporting his charities, including the Invictus Games, which are due to be held in Birmingham next year. There have been reports that Meghan is considering a return to acting. Disputes about Prince Harry and Meghan’s security in the UK remain unresolved and the letter spells out: “Any operational security issues should continue to be directed to the relevant police authorities.” Prince Harry has complained about a lack of adequate police protection in the UK, but the Palace says that has to be addressed by the Royal and VIP Executive Committee – known as Ravec – which decides security for royals and public figures. Palace sources have suggested it was better to make the Lord Chamberlain’s letter public, in a spirit of transparency, rather than risk it emerging in leaks. Prince Harry and Meghan’s representatives have been contacted for a response.

items.title: Guinée – Doko : Mystère autour de la disparition du « Kiki » d’un ressortissant burkinabè
items.description: Une affaire extraordinaire et hautement mystérieuse agite le district de Sèkè Kolita, dans la préfecture de Doko en Guinée, depuis le jeudi 3 septembre 2026. Un ressortissant burkinabè y accuse formellement un homme de la communauté Haoussa d’être parvenu, par des voies ésotériques, à faire rétrécir et disparaître son sexe, à la suite d’un banal échange de paroles et d’un simple contact sur sa moto. Entre le témoignage désespéré de la victime, désormais incapable d'uriner, et l'arrestation du suspect dans une atmosphère de vive tension, la localité oscille entre stupéfaction et psychose collective. Le district de Sèkè Kolita, d’ordinaire paisible, fait face à une agitation pour le moins inhabituelle depuis ce jeudi 3 septembre 2026. Un ressortissant burkinabè a publiquement accusé un homme présenté comme un Haoussa d’avoir mystiquement dérobé son attribut masculin, désigné localement sous le terme de « kiki » ou de « bangal ». Cette affaire hors norme a immédiatement suscité de vives interrogations au sein de la population locale, confrontée à l’un des récits les plus déroutants de l’année. Les faits se sont déroulés alors que le jeune Burkinabè venait de terminer des achats dans la localité de Gorgola. Alors qu’il s’apprêtait à envoyer un message vocal sur son téléphone, un homme s'est approché de lui avec insistance pour lui proposer des remèdes traditionnels (« médicaments »). Malgré son refus, l'inconnu s'est mis à lui parler tout en posant sa main sur sa moto. https://netafrique.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/AQNKnGARkKL2cy6MZzSSOd_sXW4KqmYKT3ZLSaDlJuUCMht91KFeHj-XNyAUzB-MA6ZAqXXIQDgGJ1NYLO6QD4KOgJrGEoD4zXaCbfCNC6gJmA.mp4 C'est à cet instant précis que la victime a été saisie d'un terrible pressentiment en réalisant que cet individu correspondait en tout point à celui qui avait déjà jeté un sort similaire à l'un de ses amis à Talamba. Pris de panique, le cœur battant à tout rompre, le jeune homme a inspecté ses vêtements pour faire une découverte effroyable : son sexe avait presque totalement disparu, se réduisant à une taille minuscule. Le témoignage de la victime décrit une situation extrêmement angoissante. Bien qu'il affirme ne ressentir aucune douleur physique directe, les conséquences de ce sortilège présumé affectent gravement ses fonctions biologiques : « Ça ne me fait pas mal, mais je ne peux même plus uriner » , déplore-t-il avec détresse. Selon ses dires, le suspect, qui est actuellement retenu, aurait lui-même revendiqué la paternité de cet acte occulte en rappelant son précédent méfait à Dalamba. Alors que la gendarmerie et les notables locaux tentent de démêler le vrai du faux dans cette affaire sensible, la population reste suspendue aux développements de l'enquête, relançant une fois de plus le débat sur la persistance de ces croyances et psychoses liées au « vol d'organes » en Afrique de l'Ouest. L’article Guinée – Doko : Mystère autour de la disparition du « Kiki » d’un ressortissant burkinabè est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: UK passport intervention: No extra charges, Tunji-Ojo clarifies
items.description: ABUJA — The Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, has clarified that Nigerians in the United Kingdom applying for international passports under the ongoing special intervention exercise are not required to pay charges beyond the official passport fees. The clarification followed concerns over inconveniences reportedly experienced by Nigerians in the UK during the application and processing of their passports. Tunji-Ojo, in a statement issued on Monday by his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Alao Babatunde, said the intervention exercise was introduced to provide Nigerians in the UK with additional options for processing their passport applications. He said the exercise did not attract any extra charges beyond the official fees of $150 for a five-year validity passport and $230 for a 10-year validity passport, exclusive of bank charges. “Neither the Ministry of Interior nor the Nigeria Immigration Service has introduced any other charges outside the aforementioned,” the statement said. The minister said consultations were ongoing with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to address the challenges being experienced by applicants and ensure that the inconveniences did not persist. According to him, the government remains committed to providing succour to Nigerians at home and abroad. The statement said applicants could also take advantage of the contactless biometric passport application system, which it described as seamless. The statement was signed by Babatunde and dated September 7, 2026. The post UK passport intervention: No extra charges, Tunji-Ojo clarifies appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Former GPHA Director-General Edward K. Osei receives Honorary Doctorate, Excellence Award
items.description: Ghanaian legal practitioner and former Director -General of the Ghana Ports and Harbors Authority (GPHA), Edward K. Osei, has been conferred with two prestigious international honors in New Delhi, India, in recognition of a career spanning international corporate law, higher education, and transformative public service, On Saturday, September 5, at the Speaker Hall of the Constitution Club of India, the Socrates Social Research University awarded Mr. Osei the Innovative Education Excellence Award 2026 alongside an Honorary Doctorate Degree in Social Service (Honoris Causa). The dual honors recognize his lifelong dedication to education, cross-border legal practice, and his public service contributions in both the United States and Ghana. Mr. Osei’s recognition highlights an impressive academic and professional journey. Holding six degrees, including a Juris Doctor (J.D.) from Temple University Beasley School of Law, an LL.M. in Taxation from New York University (NYU) School of Law, an M.B.A. from Stanford Graduate School of Business, and an M.A. from Yale University. He stands as one of West Africa’s most highly qualified cross-border corporate legal practitioners. Before entering public leadership in Ghana, Mr. Osei spent years in corporate strategy and law in the United States. His career includes corporate strategy roles at PepsiCo, Bristol-Myers Squibb, AstraZeneca, and Eastman Kodak, followed by high-stakes transactional and M&A legal practice at Boies, Schiller and Flexner LLP and as a partner at Osei and Nelson in New Jersey. He also served on the faculty at Delaware Law School (Widener University), where he taught courses in Contracts, Mergers and Acquisitions, and Taxation. In April 2017, President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo appointed Mr. Osei as Director of the Port of Tema, West Africa’s primary commercial gateway, and later as Acting Director-General of the Ghana Ports and Harbors Authority (GPHA) in June 2018. During his tenure, Mr. Osei was pivotal in modernizing Ghana’s maritime sector, most notably helping pioneer the implementation of the paperless port-clearance and joint-inspection system launched in September 2017. His operational reforms yielded immediate structural results, delivering a 24 percent increase in Tema Port revenue alongside a 20 percent improvement in vessel turnaround time. Under his direction, cargo throughput expanded from 14 million tonnes in 2017 to 16 million tonnes in 2018, accompanied by a 23.8 percent surge in transit trade serving landlocked neighbors Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger. He simultaneously reinforced operational integrity across the port by expanding CCTV infrastructure, bolstering joint security protocols, and taking direct measures to curb fraud and cargo pilferage. These achievements earned widespread industry acclaim, with Tema Port’s Golden Jubilee Terminal named Terminal of the Year at the 2018 Ghana Shippers Awards, alongside international recognition for container productivity at the African Port Awards. Currently, Mr. Osei serves as a Partner at Kaveti International Law Firm, advising clients across its New York, London, and Hyderabad platform on cross-border transactions, investment, trade, and legal cooperation, and as a Partner at Darko Law Firm in Accra, Ghana. His extensive leadership extends to statutory boards and corporate governance, having previously served as Chairman of the Ghana Dock Labour Company and Chairman of the Board of the National Homeownership Fund in Accra. The Socrates Social Research University’s recognition in New Delhi stands as a testament to Mr. Edward K. Osei’s dynamic leadership, bridging the worlds of academia, law, corporate strategy, and national development.

items.title: 11 feared killed as Boko Haram attacks Adamawa community
items.description: YOLA — No fewer than 11 people were feared killed on Monday after suspected Boko Haram insurgents invaded Zaranga village in Gombi Local Government Area of Adamawa State. A resident, who spoke to PUNCH Online on the telephone but asked not to be named because he was not authorised to speak to journalists, said the attackers invaded the community in the early hours of Monday, shooting residents and setting houses ablaze. “For now, 11 dead bodies have been recovered. Many people are still missing. Search teams and security personnel are in the forest searching for the missing people,” the resident said. Another resident said his wife and two other family members were among those killed in the attack. “My wife and two of my family members were also killed during the early morning invasion of my village,” he said. Efforts to obtain confirmation from the Adamawa State Police Command were unsuccessful as the command’s Public Relations Officer, SP Suleiman Nguroje, did not respond to calls placed to his telephone. As of the time of filing this report, the police spokesperson had yet to respond to the calls. The number of casualties could not be independently verified, while details of the attack and the whereabouts of those reported missing remained unclear. items.title: Burkina: des produits saisis, des magasins fermés
items.description: (Ipelcé, le 7 septembre 2026) Ce lundi, une équipe de la Direction régionale de l’Industrie, du Commerce et de l’Artisanat du Nazinon (DRICA-Nazinon) a mené une mission de contrôle ciblée sur les prix et la qualité des produits de grande consommation dans la commune rurale d’Ipelcé. Cette opération s’inscrit dans le cadre des actions continues de protection des consommateurs, de régulation des marchés et de préservation du pouvoir d’achat des ménages, dans un contexte marqué par des tensions sur le coût de la vie et les produits de première nécessité. À l’issue des inspections, les contrôleurs ont constaté plusieurs infractions à la réglementation commerciale, notamment le non-affichage des prix, la mise en vente de produits périmés ou prohibés ainsi que des pratiques avérées de spéculation tarifaire. Face à ces irrégularités, l’équipe de contrôle a procédé à la saisie et au retrait du marché des produits incriminés. Par ailleurs, une mesure conservatoire d’arrêt d’activité avec fermeture immédiate a été ordonnée à l’encontre d’un établissement commercial pour non-respect des prix homologués. Les contrevenants s’exposent à des sanctions administratives et pénales, conformément aux lois en vigueur. La DRICA-Nazinon saisit cette occasion pour inviter l’ensemble des acteurs économiques de la commune au respect scrupuleux de la réglementation commerciale en vigueur au Burkina Faso. Elle réaffirme sa détermination à maintenir et à intensifier les contrôles inopinés sur l’ensemble du territoire régional. items.title: Fire rips through factory in Karachi's Landhi Export Processing Zone, 3 suffer minor injuries
items.description: At least three people suffered minor injuries from smoke inhalation after a blaze ripped through a clothing factory in Karachi’s Landhi Export Processing Zone (EPZ) on Monday, Rescue 1122 said. The blaze caused part of the factory to collapse and spread to an adjacent factory, confirmed the Rescue 1122 spokesperson Hassaan Ul Haseeb Khan. However, due to timely evacuation, no loss of life was reported. The fire, which broke out around noon, continued into the night, with more than a dozen fire tenders engaged in extinguishing the blaze. Screengrab from a video shows a fire engulfing a factory in Karachi’s Landhi area on Sept 7, 2026. — Courtesy of Rescue 1122 The spokesperson told Dawn that the control room received a report of a fire at the factory at around 12:53pm. The factory imported used clothes, which were reconditioned and sold in the market. He said a large number of workers were present when the fire broke out, but they managed to evacuate safely on their own. However, when firefighters arrived, seven workers were still trapped inside. Rescue teams subsequently evacuated them safely. “Of them, three became unconscious after inhaling smoke, but they did not sustain any burn injuries and were provided first aid at the scene,” he said. Khan elaborated that the factory comprised a ground floor and three upper storeys and that the entire building was engulfed in flames. “Continued exposure to the fire and heat caused extensive damage to the structure, with around 50 per cent of the building collapsing and the remaining portion sustaining damage.” He added that the intensity of the fire caused it to spread to an adjacent factory whose building was also engulfed in flames, resulting in serious structural damage. The spokesperson said 16 fire tenders from Rescue 1122, the KMC Fire Brigade and the EPZ’s own firefighting setup were engaged in controlling the blaze, which was still raging. The rescue official further said the exact cause of the fire would be ascertained after a proper investigation once the blaze had been brought under control. However, all the goods stored in both factories were destroyed. Screengrab from a video shows a fire engulfing a factory in Karachi’s Landhi area on Sept 7, 2026. — Courtesy of Rescue 1122 Edhi ambulances and volunteers also reached the site to aid in the rescue operation, the Edhi Foundation said. Fires frequently erupt in buildings across Pakistan due to a mix of poor infrastructure, weak enforcement of safety regulations, and widespread negligence. Many structures lack proper fire exits, alarms, and emergency protocols, while faulty wiring and overloaded power systems increase the risk of electrical short circuits. The Gul Plaza inferno , which erupted on the night of January 17 at the mall, claimed at least 73 lives . The blaze took nearly two days to be fully extinguished and left over 1,100 shops in ruins. In early February, a massive fire in a plastic factory at Landhi EPZ had engulfed several nearby factories and took major firefighting efforts to be brought under control after 13 hours. Days later, a fire erupted in a high-rise building near Karachi’s Baloch Colony, with around 150 people evacuated . On February 17, a fire at a chemical factory in the SITE Industrial Area was brought under control. The next month, a blaze that broke out in Imtiaz Superstore’s Zamzama branch was brought under control after hours-long efforts by rescue officials. In June, hundreds of people were evacuated as a fire erupted in the cold storage of a department store situated in a mega shopping mall on Rashid Minhas Road in Federal B Area.

items.title: 29 Players to commence Black Starlets preparations ahead of 2026 WAFU U-17 Championship
items.description: Twenty-nine players have been handed call-ups to begin preparations for Ghana’s participation in the 2026 WAFU Zone B U-17 Championship, following an extensive talent identification and screening exercise conducted by Black Starlets coach Kasim Ocansey Mingle. The selected players emerged from a series of scouting and screening exercises organized across the country as Coach Mingle and his technical team searched for promising talents from the 2010-year group. The 29 players will now commence preparations for the 2026 WAFU Zone B U-17 Championship, where Ghana will be seeking to emerge as one of the two teams that secure qualification to the 2027 Africa U-17 Cup of Nations. The WAFU Zone B U-17 Championship, which will be held in October in Ouagadougou, also serves as the qualifying tournament for the 2027 U-17 AFCON, with only the two finalists earning tickets to the continental tournament. Coach Mingle’s selection follows a structured scouting process that took his technical team to various parts of the country in search of players capable of competing at the highest youth level. Competition for places in the final squad is expected to remain intense as the selected players seek to impress the coaches during training and subsequent assessment matches. Ghana’s qualification for the 2027 U-17 AFCON will depend on the Black Starlets’ performance at the WAFU Zone B Championship, making the upcoming regional tournament a crucial first test for Coach Mingle’s young side.

items.title: Sacrilège à Daloa en Côte d’Ivoire : Une tombe profanée à Lekaboua, le corps retrouvé sans tête ni sexe
items.description: Un acte d’une barbarie inqualifiable secoue la sous-préfecture de Gboguhé depuis ce lundi 7 septembre 2026. Dans la nuit, des individus non identifiés ont forcé une tombe du cimetière du village de Lekaboua pour en extraire le corps d'un défunt, avant de l’amputer de sa tête et de ses organes génitaux. Cette profanation d'une violence inouïe, manifestement dictée par des motivations occultes et fétichistes, a plongé les villageois et les chefs traditionnels dans la consternation et la peur. Alors que la gendarmerie nationale s'est dépêchée sur les lieux pour ouvrir une enquête d’urgence, la communauté réclame des mesures immédiates pour sécuriser la demeure de leurs ancêtres. La stupeur a saisi le village de Lekaboua, une petite localité paisible située à une vingtaine de kilomètres de Daloa, dans la région du Haut-Sassandra. Ce lundi 7 septembre 2026, au petit matin, des villageois se rendant au cimetière ont fait une découverte macabre qui a instantanément figé le sang de la communauté. Une sépulture venait d’être vandalisée. À quelques pas de la fosse fraîchement retournée gisait le corps exhumé du défunt, gisant hors de sa dernière demeure. Mais c'est l'état du cadavre qui a provoqué l'effroi général : la dépouille avait été sauvagement mutilée, dépouillée de sa tête et de ses attributs sexuels. Le spectre terrifiant des rituels fétichistes Pour l'ensemble des habitants, la nature des mutilations ne laisse que très peu de place au doute. Les soupçons se tournent immédiatement vers des pratiques de sorcellerie ou de fétichisme mystique. Dans la sous-région, l'usage de morceaux de corps humains — particulièrement les extrémités et les organes reproducteurs — demeure parfois associé à des rituels de puissance, d'enrichissement ou à des sacrifices occultes. « C'est un acte d'une barbarie inqualifiable. On n'a jamais vu ça ici. C'est une abomination » , s’indigne un habitant du village, encore sous le coup d'un traumatisme partagé par les hommes, les femmes et les chefs traditionnels. Pour cette communauté profondément attachée au culte des ancêtres, profaner une tombe est perçu comme le pire des sacrilèges, une rupture violente avec les traditions spirituelles les plus sacrées. Aujourd'hui, l'inquiétude se mêle à la colère. « On a peur pour nos morts et pour nos vivants » , confie un autre résident, résumant l'angoisse qui s'est emparée des foyers de Lekaboua. Face à la gérante de la mémoire bafouée et à la gravité des faits, les autorités villageoises et la population ont immédiatement alerté les forces de l’ordre. Des éléments de la gendarmerie nationale se sont rapidement rendus sur les lieux du sinistre pour réaliser les premières constatations d'usage et engager officiellement les investigations. Alors que l'enquête s'accélère pour identifier et appréhender les auteurs de cette profanation odieuse qui courent toujours dans la nature, les habitants de Lekaboua lancent un appel solennel à la vigilance collective. Ils réclament un éclairage et une sécurisation pérenne du cimetière du village pour empêcher que de tels outrages ne se reproduisent et pour que leurs disparus puissent enfin reposer en paix. L’article Sacrilège à Daloa en Côte d'Ivoire : Une tombe profanée à Lekaboua, le corps retrouvé sans tête ni sexe est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Pakistan at ‘very start’ of Test rebuilding process, says bowling coach Noffke
items.description: Pakistan are at the “very start” of rebuilding their Test side, bowling coach Ashley Noffke said on Monday, as the team attempts to move past a tumultuous week that has seen sweeping changes to the squad and a shake-up of its coaching staff. “Every nation has a life cycle, and there’ll be moments where they play really great cricket for long periods and then older players will move out and younger players will come in. And we’re at the very start of that process,” Noffke told reporters at Edgbaston. The contrast with England, who are attempting to complete a 3-0 series sweep after emphatic victories at Headingley and Lord’s, could hardly be starker. While Pakistan have brought in a new interim head coach in Mike Hesson, made wholesale changes to their squad and sent Noffke to England at short notice, the hosts have been able to build on a settled pace attack led by Jofra Archer, who says he is finally enjoying a period of stability after years of injury. Pakistan’s changes have opened the door for young fast bowlers Razaullah and Mohammad Imran Jr, with Noffke viewing their presence in England as part of a longer-term plan rather than simply an emergency response to two defeats. “They’re young guys. They haven’t experienced England conditions and they’re over here to learn and grow,” he said. “I think with any life cycle of any cricket team, you need to take a forward-thinking approach to what we might need in the future. I think other teams have been doing that and it’s now our turn to bring young guys over, make sure they get accustomed to conditions that are different to theirs at home.” Both bowlers offer Pakistan something that has been missing from their attack during the series — pace. Noffke said they were “certainly closer to the 140 mark” than some of the quicks Pakistan had previously used. Imran Jr, a left-armer, and Razaullah, a right-armer with a different action, could also provide variety to an attack that has relied heavily on veteran seamer Mohammad Abbas. “Abbas has obviously bowled amazingly through this series and we need to support him as best we can,” Noffke said. Noffke himself was thrust into the Test set-up at short notice, saying he received a message “at 3am” informing him that management was sending him to England. Asked whether he had been given an explanation for the sweeping changes to the squad, he said: “Not really.” “It’s not my job to be in consultation with where they see who’s in and who’s out. That’s obviously the selection panel,” he said. “As we’ve already asked Mike [Hesson] in previous interviews, he’s only just come into that phase. So, like we said before, it’s unsettling, but it’s about getting on with it, focusing on what’s ahead of us as a Test-playing squad and trying to develop in all areas.” The uncertainty surrounding Pakistan has also been compounded by an internal PCB disciplinary inquiry into the conduct of some players announced on Monday. Noffke said he knew no more about the matter than the media did. “As much as you do. And I can be really honest in that — I don’t know too much,” he said. “I sit outside of that decision-making model above us as coaches.” He said the coaching staff had attempted to keep the players focused on the cricket rather than the developments surrounding them. “There’s obviously a feeling of uncertainty, but they’ve just got back on the job,” Noffke said. “I’ve been really impressed with the level of calmness that they’ve taken over the last couple of days once we’ve given them time to talk.” The Australian said Pakistan’s immediate strategy was straightforward: “good Test cricket”, discipline, bowling in good areas and building long partnerships with the bat. Asked whether Pakistan risked becoming a laughing stock following the events on and off the field and whether the team needed to restore some pride, Noffke said performances were the only meaningful answer. “Well, you only install pride with really good cricket, don’t you?” he said. “There’s no question that we need to develop our game. Our Test game needs to improve. But that doesn’t mean that we should be worried about that.” England, meanwhile, are preparing for the possibility of completing a clean sweep with a fast-bowling unit that has been one of the defining features of the series. Archer, who returned to Test cricket in July last year after more than four years away, believes he is now in a “good place” following a succession of career-threatening injuries. The Barbados-born quick arrived in England in 2015 and four years later spearheaded the attack during England’s dramatic World Cup triumph at Lord’s, while also starring in the 2019 Ashes. But an elbow problem subsequently developed, followed by back injuries, and Archer was sidelined from Test cricket from February 2021 until July 2025. The 31-year-old, who continues to play all three international formats, said his long periods away from the game had also brought unexpected benefits. “The time when I was injured, I really got away from cricket,” he told the BBC on Monday. “It’s all been a blur. I didn’t realise how long the time out was, either.” Archer said the enforced breaks allowed him to spend more time at home in Barbados after moving to England. “I got to spend some time at home, because, moving over, I never really got more than a couple of weeks,” he said. “To spend a month here and there, it was really nice.” “I’d be lying if I didn’t say I had a good time away from everything. Now, everything is really nice. My body is in a good place, the team is in a good place and everyone is in a good place. I just want to play cricket.” Archer has played a key role in England’s two victories over Pakistan and will be central to their bid for a 3-0 result at Edgbaston. His presence has also added further weight to an England pace attack featuring Ollie Robinson, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson, with the group beginning to draw comparisons with England’s celebrated “Fab Four” of Matthew Hoggard, Steve Harmison, Simon Jones and Andrew Flintoff, who helped secure the 2005 Ashes. Pakistan, by contrast, are still deciding whether to field four seamers or retain a spinner, with Noffke saying the decision would depend on the pitch and weather. “We’ve got some really good options now to select in terms of the four seamers, our spinner that can bat. There are some great selection dilemmas, which is nice,” he said. The Edgbaston pitch has plenty of grass, but Noffke expects it to be a good surface. “It looks a good surface. There’s plenty of grass on it, though,” he said. For Pakistan, however, the significance of Wednesday’s Test extends beyond avoiding a series whitewash. With new faces being introduced amid considerable upheaval, Edgbaston could offer an early glimpse of the side Noffke believes is only now beginning the process of rebuilding.

items.title: 2027: Aiyedatiwa denies sponsoring opposition candidates
items.description: …Insists: I’ve not asked any candidate to contest under another party By Dayo Johnson, Akure AKURE — Ondo State Governor, Hon. Lucky Aiyedatiwa, has denied allegations that he is involved in anti-party activities following the substitution of his preferred National Assembly candidates by the national leadership of the All Progressives Congress (APC). Aiyedatiwa spoke on Monday at a stakeholders’ meeting with APC local government and ward chairmen in Akure. The governor described those spreading the allegations as “naysayers, blackmailers and slanderers” and declared zero tolerance for anti-party activities ahead of the 2027 general elections. He said reports that he was sponsoring candidates of other political parties in retaliation against the APC leadership were false. “I have zero tolerance for anti-party. I have never engaged in anti-party in my life,” he declared. “I have not asked any candidate to contest in any other party.” The governor traced his political loyalty to the progressive political bloc, recalling that even when the Labour Party and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) were dominant in his senatorial district, he chose to join the Alliance for Democracy (AD)/Action Congress of Nigeria (ACN). He also recounted his experience during the 2019 APC governorship primary, when he said he won the exercise but the national leadership overturned the result. “The party leadership was supreme. That experience taught me the need for members to respect the authority and decisions of the leadership,” he said. Aiyedatiwa urged the 18 local government and 203 ward chairmen to mobilise at the grassroots and work towards victory for the APC in 2027. “Elections are won at the polling units. And the polling units are right there in the ward. And you are the ward chairmen. You are occupying a significant role in party structure,” he said. He directed ward chairmen and secretaries to hold regular meetings to deliberate on party affairs, stressing that mobilisation must not be mixed with anti-party activities. “So, no to anti-party. Let’s support Mr President and all the candidates of our party,” he added. The state APC Chairman, Hon. Babatunde Kolawole, called for total loyalty to the governor and the party. Kolawole said the governor had directed the party to secure 100 per cent support for all APC candidates. He warned that the party had gathered intelligence on acts of disloyalty and that those found culpable would face consequences. The chairman commended Aiyedatiwa for activating the party’s organs and approving a 100 per cent increase in allowances for ward and local government chairmen as well as state executives. Speaking on behalf of the local government chairmen, Oluwadare Fadumo, thanked the governor for what he described as unprecedented support for councils, market women and youths. “We want to thank you because this is the first time this is happening in the history of politics in Ondo State,” Fadumo said. The governor said the commendations for his administration’s projects were encouraging and would spur the government to fast-track ongoing projects. items.title: 2027: They may discount us, but our votes will count — Makinde
items.description: …Clears the air on petrol pricing …Says: ‘Government must show its workings’ …Peter Obi says Makinde qualified to be president …Not every candidate is electable – Daura …‘Disregard us at your own peril’ – Bala Mohammed …Dantalle: ‘Reset Nigeria’ begins By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples’ Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, on Monday fired back at those dismissing his 2027 presidential bid, saying they could not discount millions of Nigerians whose votes would determine the country’s political future. Makinde spoke in Abuja while commissioning the APM presidential campaign headquarters, where he unveiled the ‘Reset Nigeria’ campaign, built around transparency in government, accountability and ensuring that the country’s resources translate into better lives for citizens. Makinde also clarified his position on petrol pricing, saying he was not advocating a return to the old fuel subsidy regime but wanted Nigerians to benefit more directly from the crude oil produced in the country. He argued that the benefit should be built into the price at which crude is supplied to local refineries, rather than through interventions after costs and inefficiencies have accumulated across the petroleum value chain. “So why should crude oil supplied to Nigerian refineries be priced as though Nigeria does not produce crude oil?” Makinde asked. He called for transparency across production, domestic crude allocation, refining, transportation, distribution, taxes and retail margins, saying Nigerians should be able to understand how the final pump price is determined. ‘Government must show its workings’ Makinde said the principle extended beyond the petroleum sector to the way government makes decisions and manages public resources. “It means that government must show its workings. It means that Nigerians must know how decisions are made, how public resources are used and who benefits from them,” he said. He said the campaign would reach Nigerians whose daily experiences shape the impact of government policies, including traders, farmers, workers, business owners and young people. Makinde recalled that when he first contested the Oyo governorship, many had dismissed his chances of winning. “They may discount one candidate. But they cannot discount millions of Nigerians united behind a better future,” he said. He urged Nigerians to make the campaign a broader civic conversation rather than one restricted to politicians. “Ask questions. Challenge our ideas. Share your own ideas. Organise within your communities. Become a resetter. “We count. Our voices count. Our experiences count. Our ideas count. And, together, our votes will count,” Makinde said. Makinde qualified to contest presidency, says Peter Obi Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, attended the commissioning, said Makinde was qualified to contest the presidency and that Nigerians should be allowed to freely choose their leaders. “Yes, Seyi Makinde is qualified to contest for President. What we are doing today is to show you that, for us, we don’t have desperation. We want the people of Nigeria to make their choice. Whoever they choose, all of us will come together to build a new Nigeria,” Obi said. He added that political competition should centre on solving the problems confronting Nigerians rather than deepening divisions. “Let our quarrel be to feed our people. Let our quarrel be to pull our people out of poverty. We want a Nigeria where a child of nobody can be somebody without knowing anybody,” he said. Daura: Not every candidate is electable APM vice-presidential candidate, Lawal Daura, urged Nigerians to distinguish between candidates who are legally qualified to contest and those capable of winning an election. “There are candidates that may be eligible, but they are not electable. I want Nigerians to be able to distinguish that,” Daura said. He also urged opposition parties to campaign on issues rather than attack one another, saying their cooperation should be directed at producing what he described as a “qualitative opposition”. “We are all together. We want to provide a very qualitative opposition. And that qualitative opposition is supposed to be beneficial to all Nigerians,” he said. Bala Mohammed: ‘Disregard us at your own peril’ APM National Leader and Bauchi State Governor, Bala Mohammed, said the commissioning of the headquarters demonstrated the party’s seriousness about the 2027 election. “Whoever disregards us is doing it at his own peril,” Mohammed warned. He praised Makinde’s record in Oyo State, as well as his experience in the private sector and oil and gas industry, saying these qualities positioned him to reset the country. Mohammed also stressed the need for party loyalty, supremacy of the party and harmony among its members, urging Nigerians to put the country first. Dantalle: ‘Reset Nigeria’ begins APM National Chairman, Yusuf Mamman Dantalle, described the commissioning as the beginning of the party’s campaign to ‘Reset Nigeria’, saying the headquarters would serve as its campaign base for the 2027 election. He said the crowd at the event reflected what he described as Nigerians’ yearning for competence, courage, compassion and accountability, while presenting the APM ticket as a viable alternative. Dantalle said the campaign would focus on solutions rather than political bitterness, adding that Makinde’s record in Oyo State and Daura’s security background offered complementary strengths for the presidency. “On a rescue mission, there is no time for frivolities. Citizens are tired and weary of politics of bitterness, division and hatred that impedes the nation’s democracy,” Dantalle said. He urged Nigerians to support APM candidates across the country. ‎ The post 2027: They may discount us, but our votes will count — Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: US Green Card Lottery: Full list of countries excluded from programme
items.description: The US Diversity Visa, popularly known as the Green Card Lottery, excludes nationals of a number of countries each year based on their recent levels of immigration to the US. For the DV-2026 programme , natives of 20 countries were not eligible to participate, according to the US Department of State. The Diversity Visa programme makes immigrant visas available to people from countries with historically low rates of immigration to the United States. Under US law, countries from which more than 50,000 natives immigrated to the US over the previous five years are generally excluded from the programme. Full list of countries excluded from DV-2026 The US Department of State listed the following countries as ineligible for the DV-2026 programme: Bangladesh Brazil Canada China, including Hong Kong SAR Colombia Cuba Dominican Republic El Salvador Haiti Honduras India Jamaica Mexico Nigeria Pakistan Philippines South Korea Venezuela Vietnam The list was published by the US Department of State in its DV-2026 information. Why are these countries excluded? The Diversity Visa programme is designed to encourage immigration from countries that have historically sent relatively few immigrants to the United States. Under the programme’s rules, countries with high levels of recent immigration can become ineligible. The list can therefore change from one Diversity Visa programme year to another depending on immigration figures. The exclusion does not mean that citizens of these countries are generally banned from travelling to or immigrating to the United States. Rather, people born in the listed countries cannot normally enter the Diversity Visa lottery for that particular programme year. Nigeria among the excluded countries Nigeria is one of the countries that has repeatedly been excluded from the Diversity Visa programme because of its relatively high level of immigration to the United States. For Nigerians hoping to obtain US permanent residence, this means the Diversity Visa Lottery is not an available immigration route while Nigeria remains on the exclusion list. However, Nigerians may still qualify for other US immigration pathways, including family-sponsored and employment-based immigrant visas, subject to the relevant eligibility requirements. items.title: Irán afirma que la “era de las respuestas proporcionales” a Estados Unidos ha terminado

Según han anunciado varios altos responsables de la República Islámica, el país asiático ha dejado a un lado la doctrina defensiva para adoptar una nueva estrategia en la que “cualquier agresión contra los intereses y la seguridad de Irán recibirá una respuesta más rápida, más fuerte y más dolorosa”, advirtió hace días el presidente del Parlamento y líder negociador iraní, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf. items.title: U-20 Women’s World Cup: Sampson demands response after ‘cheap’ goals cost Ghana
items.description: “Cheap.” That’s how Black Princesses head coach Charles Sampson described the goals his side conceded in their opening game defeat to Ecuador at the FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland. Ghana conceded two early goals before Ecuador put the final nail in the coffin with a third in the second half, leaving the Black Princesses to begin their campaign with a defeat. Sampson was far from pleased with his side’s performance and has called for a much-improved outing in their next game. “The way we conceded the opening two goals was cheap. It created an imbalance and allowed Ecuador to have the upper hand. “However, I liked the attitude my girls showed in response to going down. We were unfortunate at times and not clinical enough at other times, and that allowed them to finish the game off with a counter-attack. “We have to accept the result and come back stronger in our next game.” Ghana will face Korea in their next group game on Wednesday, with the Black Princesses targeting a positive result to revive their hopes of progressing to the knockout stage.
